value.first: He's 6 months, so now is the time. I'd do iron-first solids with early-and-often allergen introduction: his stored iron runs low around now, and trials show waiting on allergens backfires - early, regular peanut cut allergy by about 80%. Day 1: when he's rested and a bit hungry, sit him upright in a high chair and offer a spoon or two of iron-fortified oat cereal mixed with his milk. Most lands on the tray. That's a win.
value.second: Days 2-7: build to iron-rich food twice a day, add mashed veg and fruit, milk as usual. Week 2, peanut: one morning, thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter with warm water, give a tiny taste, wait 10 minutes, then the rest, and watch him two hours. A day or so later, hard-scrambled egg the same way. Then one new allergen a day: yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, fish. Keep each about twice a week after.
value.third: Gagging is noisy and normal; choking is silent. Lumpy and soft finger foods by 9 months. No honey, no whole nuts, no globs of nut butter. If you'd rather skip purees, baby-led weaning is the finger-food version. It's working when he takes some iron food twice a day and allergens stay in rotation. A few hives or vomiting after a new food: stop it and see your provider before offering it again. I'll check in Friday.
